title: False Friends in Automotive Manufacturing & Assembly
description: Master deceptive cognates (false friends) frequently misused by Czech manufacturing engineers, line operators, and quality inspectors in automotive production.

questions.prompt: Before clearing the Tatra Force chassis for the test track, the technician must thoroughly _____ the torque on all hub nuts.

explanations.correct: 'Check' (or 'inspect / verify') means to examine something to ensure it is accurate, safe, or working properly.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Control' means to direct, dominate, or regulate (e.g., 'the ECU controls the fuel injection'), NOT to visually examine or measure.
explanations.wrong_C: 'Command' means to give orders, inappropriate for torque verification.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Steer' means to guide directional heading, unrelated to bolt torque.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'kontrolovat' translates to 'check', 'inspect', or 'verify'. Using 'control' here is one of the most widespread Czenglish mistakes in Czech factories.

questions.prompt: Our Kopřivnice heavy machinery plant does not simply assemble parts; we _____ our own backbone tubes and swinging half-axles in-house.

explanations.correct: 'Manufacture' (or 'produce') is the standard professional term for industrial production of goods and mechanical parts.
explanations.wrong_A: While 'fabricate' in heavy industry can mean metal structural fabrication, in general English it often means 'to falsify / make up an excuse or lie'. 'Manufacture' is clearer and unambiguous.
explanations.wrong_B: 'Invent' means to devise a new concept, not the physical routine production of components.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Pretend' means to simulate or make believe.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czechs sometimes use 'fabricate' thinking of 'továrna / fabrika'. In industrial contexts, stick to 'manufacture' or 'produce' to avoid connotations of falsification.

questions.prompt: The quality department maintains detailed digital _____ of every welding inspection carried out on the assembly line.

explanations.correct: 'Records' (or 'logs / documentation') refers to recorded facts, historical data, and audit tracking in manufacturing.
explanations.wrong_B: 'Evidence' is an uncountable noun predominantly used in criminal law or scientific hypotheses (důkazní materiál), not standard quality logs.
explanations.wrong_C: 'Proofs' is usually uncountable ('proof') or refers to mathematical demonstrations and printing proofs.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Clues' refers to hints used in detective investigations.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'evidence' (e.g. 'evidence zakázek / evidence svárů') translates to 'records', 'tracking', or 'logs'. In English, 'evidence' means courtroom proof.

questions.prompt: What is the _____ production capacity of the cab paint shop following last month's robotics upgrade?

explanations.correct: 'Current' means happening or existing now (současný / nynější).
explanations.wrong_A: 'Actual' means real/fact-based as opposed to theoretical or estimated (skutečný/faktický), not 'current/now'.
explanations.wrong_B: 'Eventual' means happening at the end after a delay (konečný / budoucí), not 'now'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'aktuální' translates to 'current' or 'present', NOT 'actual'. In English, 'actual' means 'real / in fact'.

questions.prompt: During the ultrasonic non-destructive testing, the technician detected a minor metallurgical _____ in the forging.

explanations.correct: 'Flaw' (or 'defect / fissure') refers to a physical imperfection, crack, or blemish in a material.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Deficiency' refers to a lack of an essential quality or nutrient (e.g., vitamin deficiency, dietary lack), not a material crack.
explanations.wrong_B: 'Absence' means the state of being away.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Shortage' means an insufficient quantity of supply.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czechs sometimes translate 'defekt / vada materiálu' as 'deficiency'. The proper technical terms are 'flaw', 'defect', or 'imperfection'.

questions.prompt: Our line managers regularly meet to coordinate _____ shifts and ensure seamless handover between morning and afternoon teams.

explanations.correct: 'Consecutive' means following continuously in unbroken or logical sequence (po sobě jdoucí).
explanations.wrong_A: 'Concurrent' means occurring at the exact same time (souběžný), which morning and afternoon shifts do not.

questions.cz_learning_point: Do not confuse 'consecutive' (následující po sobě) with 'concurrent' (probíhající současně ve stejný okamžik).

questions.prompt: The workshop supervisor asked the apprentice to _____ the specialized pneumatic torque wrench to station 4.

explanations.correct: 'Bring' means to carry or lead something toward the speaker/destination.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Fetch' means go and bring back, but 'bring to station 4' is standard.
explanations.wrong_B: 'Conduct' means to manage, guide, or transmit electricity, not to physically carry a tool (Czech 'donést' vs 'vést').
explanations.wrong_C: 'Translate' means to render into another language (Czech 'přeložit', not carry).

questions.cz_learning_point: Avoid confusing false Latin cognates like 'conduct' (provádět audit, vést proud) with basic physical movement of items ('bring', 'deliver').

questions.prompt: All hazardous assembly chemicals must be stored in _____ containers to prevent toxic evaporation.

explanations.correct: 'Airtight' is the natural, modern English term for preventing the entry or escape of air and vapors.
explanations.wrong_B: While 'hermetic' exists, it is overly archaic or used in specialized seals ('hermetically sealed'); 'airtight' is preferred.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Insulated' refers to thermal or electrical barrier protection, not gas sealing.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'hermetický' is often rendered as 'airtight' or 'sealed' in modern technical manufacturing English.

questions.prompt: Before installing the planetary reduction gearbox, the mechanic ensured that all mating surfaces were _____ and free of burrs.

explanations.correct: 'Smooth' (having an even and regular surface free of roughness or burrs) is the proper mechanical term.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Flat' refers to planar geometry, but 'free of burrs' relates directly to surface finish smoothness.
explanations.wrong_C: 'Plane' is a geometric concept or tool, not an adjective for surface finish quality.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Slick' implies slippery (e.g., icy road), not machined finish.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'hladký' translates to 'smooth'; do not confuse 'plane / flat' with surface texture finish.

questions.prompt: Our quality assurance manual strictly forbids operators from making _____ modifications to standard operating procedures.

explanations.correct: 'Arbitrary' (based on random choice or personal whim rather than system rule) accurately reflects unauthorized changes.
explanations.wrong_B: 'Voluntary' means done of one's own free will without payment or force (dobrovolný).
